originalTitle: Stock boom is fueling a ‘retirement party,’ economists say — what it means for workers
summary: Stocks have surged, and economists said the resulting "wealth effect" has led older workers to retire at a faster clip.
content:
The stock market boom seems to be fueling a wave of retirements .

Workers age 55 and older are leaving the labor force at a rapid pace, government data shows, a trend that coincides with ballooning stock wealth fueled by euphoria over artificial intelligence .

The retirement surge among these workers is attributable in part to a "wealth effect," economists said: Workers near traditional retirement age have seen their stock portfolios swell and feel rich enough to finally leave their 9-to-5.

In a research note last month, Bank of America economists referred to the trend as a "stock-fueled retirement party."

"Labor force participation is collapsing among older workers," wrote the economists, Stephen Juneau and Aditya Bhave. "We think the strength of the equity market is partly to blame."

Workforce exits among older workers have helped keep unemployment relatively low in recent years, economists said. Their departures help make space for job seekers and new entrants to the labor market, an important factor in an otherwise frozen job market , they said.

However, if AI optimism wanes and the stock market sours, it could mean bad news for these recent retirees, the U.S. labor market and the economy, economists said.

The labor force includes people who have a job and unemployed people who are looking for work. The labor force participation rate is the percentage of people who are in the labor force.

Participation among workers 55 years and older initially declined sharply in the early days of the Covid-19 pandemic, as it did for the broader pool of workers, too.

However, labor force participation among older workers "never recovered" after the pandemic, Bank of America economists wrote. It stayed "range-bound" until the summer of 2024, but "has taken another big leg down since then," they wrote.

Since August 2024, the labor force participation rate for workers age 55 and older has declined from 38.6% to 37.2%, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data .

Read more CNBC personal finance coverage

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 stock index yielded a string of double-digit returns for investors in recent years: 26% in 2023, 25% in 2024 and 18% in 2025, including reinvested dividends, according to data compiled by Aswath Damodaran, a finance professor at New York University.

The index is up about 16% so far in 2026, as of early Monday.

The resulting wealth surge, including in people's retirement accounts, such as 401(k) plans, likely made the choice to retire an easier one for many people, said Thomas Ryan, a North America economist at Capital Economics.

The net worth of households and nonprofits increased by $12.8 trillion, to $195.9 trillion, in the second quarter of 2026, driven primarily by strong stock returns, according to Federal Reserve data . That's by far the largest quarterly wealth increase on record since 2000, when the central bank started tracking the statistic, according to a CNBC analysis of Fed data.

"It puts people in a position where they can retire early, because they're in a favorable [financial] position," Ryan said.

Of course, near-retirees may be unlikely to be fully invested in stocks.

Financial advisors generally recommend shifting to a more conservative asset allocation leading up to and in retirement, to avoid subjecting one's whole nest egg to the volatility of the stock market.

However, the typical 65-year-old might still have a relatively large allocation to stocks — perhaps 50%, with the remainder in assets such as bonds and cash , for example. Stocks are the traditional growth engine of an investment portfolio and provide a hedge against the rising cost of living over a retirement that may last many decades.

"If people weren't feeling confident enough that they could afford to retire, they wouldn't — and we'd see a very different story in the data," said Michael Reid, head of U.S. economics at the Royal Bank of Canada.

Wealth effect compounds demographic trend

But the wealth effect isn't the only factor pushing down labor force participation among older workers.

The wealth effect compounds a broader demographic trend, economists said. A record number of people are reaching traditional retirement age: From 2024 to 2027, more than 4 million young baby boomers each year are expected to turn 65 .

The labor force participation trend is also likely partly attributable to early retirement packages, including those offered to federal workers by the so-called Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, and companies such as Microsoft , which this year offered its first-ever retirement program to U.S. workers , Reid said.

Older workers may be reluctant to withdraw from the labor force — and may even try to " unretire " — if stocks start to falter , economists said.

"What happens if we get this long-expected drawdown in the equity market, if we're in an AI bubble now and it reverses at some point?" Ryan said. "You'd potentially get some people at the margin who feel their 401(k) is in a good position now at 56, 57 years old who might come back to the labor force."

Of course, that outcome isn't a given.

Stocks have defied gravity, despite headwinds such as the Iran war.

AI has been a "powerful driver, as companies spend heavily on computing power, data centers and infrastructure, which is supporting technology, manufacturing, energy and industrials," Lisa Shalett, chief investment officer of Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, wrote in a note Wednesday.

While stocks have room to run, they face pressure heading into 2027 from higher bond yields, elevated oil prices, policy uncertainty and strain among lower-income consumers, Shalett wrote.

"The risks are becoming harder to ignore," she wrote.

A stock drawdown poses risks for retirees — especially those early in retirement who must withdraw money from their stock portfolio for income. When that happens, it's known as " sequence of returns risk ": The order, or sequence, of your gains or losses over time
chineseTitle: 经济学家称，股市繁荣正在助长“退休派对”——这对工人意味着什么
chineseSummary: 股市飙升，经济学家表示，由此产生的“财富效应”导致老年工人更快退休。
chineseContent:
股市的繁荣似乎正在引发一波退休潮。

政府数据显示，55 岁及以上的工人正在迅速离开劳动力市场，这一趋势与人工智能的狂热推动的股票财富不断膨胀同时发生。

经济学家表示，这些工人的退休人数激增部分归因于“财富效应”：接近传统退休年龄的工人看到他们的股票投资组合不断膨胀，并感觉自己足够富有，最终摆脱了朝九晚五的生活。

在上个月的一份研究报告中，美国银行经济学家将这一趋势称为“股票驱动的退休派对”。

经济学家斯蒂芬·朱诺（Stephen Juneau）和阿迪亚·巴夫（Aditya Bhave）写道：“老年工人的劳动力参与率正在下降。” “我们认为股市走强是部分原因。”

经济学家表示，近年来，老年工人的退出有助于将失业率保持在相对较低的水平。他们表示，他们的离开有助于为求职者和新进入劳动力市场的人腾出空间，这是就业市场冻结的一个重要因素。

然而，经济学家表示，如果人工智能乐观情绪减弱且股市恶化，这对这些最近退休的人员、美国劳动力市场和经济来说可能意味着坏消息。

劳动力包括有工作的人和正在寻找工作的失业者。劳动力参与率是指劳动力人口所占的百分比。

在 Covid-19 大流行初期，55 岁及以上工人的参与度最初急剧下降，更广泛的工人群体也是如此。

然而，美国银行经济学家写道，大流行之后，老年工人的劳动力参与率“从未恢复”。他们写道，直到 2024 年夏天，它一直处于“区间波动”，但“自那以后又大幅下跌”。

根据劳工统计局的数据，自 2024 年 8 月以来，55 岁及以上工人的劳动力参与率已从 38.6% 下降至 37.2%。

阅读更多 CNBC 个人理财报道

与此同时，纽约大学金融学教授阿斯瓦斯·达莫达兰(Aswath Damodaran)编制的数据显示，标准普尔500指数近年来为投资者带来了一系列两位数的回报：2023年为26%，2024年为25%，2025年为18%，其中包括再投资股息。

截至周一早间，该指数 2026 年迄今已上涨约 16%。

凯投宏观 (Capital Economics) 北美经济学家托马斯·瑞安 (Thomas Ryan) 表示，由此产生的财富激增，包括人们的退休账户（例如 401(k) 计划）的财富激增，可能会让许多人更容易做出退休的选择。

根据美联储的数据，2026 年第二季度，家庭和非营利组织的净资产增加了 12.8 万亿美元，达到 195.9 万亿美元，这主要是由强劲的股票回报率推动的。根据 CNBC 对美联储数据的分析，这是自 2000 年央行开始跟踪统计数据以来有记录以来迄今为止最大的季度财富增幅。

“这让人们可以提前退休，因为他们处于有利的[财务]状况，”瑞安说。

当然，接近退休的人可能不太可能完全投资股票。

财务顾问通常建议在退休前和退休后转向更保守的资产配置，以避免使自己的全部储蓄受到股市波动的影响。

然而，典型的 65 岁老人可能仍然有相对较大的股票配置——也许是 50%，其余的则为债券和现金等资产。股票是投资组合的传统增长引擎，可以对冲可能持续数十年的退休生活成本上升的风险。

加拿大皇家银行美国经济主管迈克尔·里德表示：“如果人们对自己有能力退休没有足够的信心，他们就不会——而且我们会在数据中看到截然不同的情况。”

财富效应加剧了人口趋势

但财富效应并不是老年工人劳动力参与率下降的唯一因素。

经济学家表示，财富效应加剧了更广泛的人口趋势。达到传统退休年龄的人数创历史新高：从 2024 年到 2027 年，每年将有超过 400 万年轻婴儿潮一代预计年满 65 岁。

里德说，劳动力参与趋势也可能部分归因于提前退休计划，包括所谓的政府效率部（DOGE）以及微软等公司向联邦工作人员提供的计划，微软今年向美国工人提供了有史以来第一个退休计划。

经济学家表示，如果股市开始下跌，老年工人可能不愿意退出劳动力市场，甚至可能试图“取消退休”。

“如果股市出现长期预期的下跌，如果我们现在处于人工智能泡沫之中，并且泡沫在某个时候逆转，会发生什么？”瑞安说。 “你可能会发现一些处于边缘的人，他们认为自己的 401(k) 计划现在处于有利地位，在 56 岁、57 岁的时候可能会重返劳动力市场。”

当然，这个结果并不是既定的。

尽管面临伊朗战争等不利因素，但股市仍不顾地心引力。

摩根士丹利财富管理公司首席投资官 Lisa Shalett 在周三的一份报告中写道，人工智能一直是“强大的驱动力，因为企业在计算能力、数据中心和基础设施上投入了大量资金，这些都支持技术、制造、能源和工业”。

沙莱特写道，虽然股市还有上涨空间，但进入 2027 年，它们将面临债券收益率上升、油价上涨、政策不确定性和低收入消费者压力等压力。

“风险变得越来越难以忽视，”她写道。
